247: Damage is decent, but insufficiently high to be of practical use anywhere. The 6 second stun can be interesting though.
248: HA scaling team wide penetration buff is very useful early on, but damage falls off drastically in end game contents.
249: Decent Ibelin abuser that also has motion speed debuffs, which can potentially be of use for bosses that doesn't have immunity to it.
250: Decent tank ignore hero with multihit, very useful in RSL but close to useless otherwise.
251: Dispels with every block, but poor damage.
252: Her debuffs aren't bad, but is not something that requires your opponent's immediate attention. Also hard countered by debuff immunity.
253: Good block gen support for a 3 chain leader and takes no investment. Granted, she doesn't provide anything other than this. Recommended for early on.
254: The activating condition is too strict for every part of his passive, and the payout is not worth the effort. The team wide 50% HA buff is nice, however.
255: Capable shield that comes with decent buff, but she can't heal.
256: Comes with heal block, so she at least is useful for that. Still not worth using though.
257: One of the worst wizards. Not recommended.
258: Seimei is a dispel hero that dispels with a long cooldown. Don't use him.
259: Debuff is workable but not needed anywhere in game as of now. Range problem makes him a strictly worse choice than other defensive healers.
263: Damage can come out instantly after activation, and can often one-shot enemies in outdated PvE contents. However, with the introduction of delegation, this niche is not much needed.
264: His damage isn't bad, but the utility is still kind of outdated in today's meta. Doesn't see much use anywhere.
265: Good periodic burst with decent hit count, but tends to get SP locked due to her incredibly long animation.
266: Penguin summons takes up no animation, chance to double cast each block, plus insane red comet and flamethrower scaling equates to one of the highest burst DPS in the game. Penetration is a problem though.
267: Damage is decent, has shred, but she is locked to lead and also happens to need a ton of 3 chains to work to her full potential. Oh, and she can't use SM so no Ibelin abuse either. These mechanics makes her team composition incredibly limiting.
268: A DPS priest designed to counter Eva, but one can proactively abuse his mechanic via low accuracy heroes seeing as he provides neutral, tank ignore damage that also happens to dispel. However, damage capability has since fell due to powercreep.
271: Ridiculous damage capability on top of a 60% DT debuff, and not hungry at all, makes her a solid choice of DPS in Total War. Viability outside of Total War is questionable as she does not move and needs to take 10 hits to start dealing good damage.
273: Has undispellable tanking and all-damage-type DT debuff, but takes 6 seconds to put this up. Requires SP accessory to be at all viable in Total War. Despite having reflect, she is not tanky enough to make good use of it in arena. May eventually see use in the future.
274: Due to her debuff immune, knockback immune, and permanent auto tanking nature, she is one of the more frequently used tanks in ordeal as she could preventing miscellaneous difficulties caused by displacements, allowing for a rather smooth experience.
276: Consistently high hit count paired with ridiculously high CC stats makes her a rather competent choice in challenge. The fact that her bullet doesn't travel fast means that the saved bullets will practically instant kill the third or fourth boss in challenge when given sufficient buffers.
277: Consistent damage and is incredibly fast to activate, making her a genuine threat in arena, especially given her near permanent airborne capability. However, damage has fell off in recent times.
278: Her damage honestly isn't bad, but she doesn't do anything too special to warrant trying to getting her in particular.
279: An unique tank killer who can easily murder high Armor opponents while dealing severe damage to backlines as well. Generally a good option to have for arena if you intend to be competitive.
280: One of the strongest and most versatile buffers in game, providing consistent and potent offensive buffs that is customizable to suit your every need. If possible, do consider obtaining multiple copies to enable different builds.
281: Imagine Morgan, but with none of the drawbacks, on top of higher damage and more hit count. Penetration is a problem though, but once you meet the requirement, he will demolish everything.
282: Neutral damage DPS with Bihwa level damage, on top of high damage amplification and CR shred, with infinite range at that. Albeit this is locked behind a strict condition, but let's be honest, where in PvE contents do you find something that DOESN'T have knockback immunity?
283: Mark damage is alright, but falls flat when compared to any of the viable DPSes nowadays.
284: Only consider him as a choice if you have Kaede or Primrose. Massive range, good burst and unique synergy with Kaede that amplifies his damage exponentially makes Altair the single fastest option for clearing challenge... but he's hard locked to Kaede
285: Flexible, consistent, and hits like a whale. Sometimes that's all you need from a character. Do note that stuns will cancel her charge.
286: Decent damage, decent hit count, and good stats on top of that. Though, the need of 2 hard 3 chain heavily slows her down, and she can have issue fighting enemy with knockback.
287: It's hard to recommend either of the twins without one another. Frederick in particular works decently well without Francesca thanks to his massive range and only needing ally blocks to work. Though, due to that, he would often be locked to a team with insane block gen.
288: Fredrick's second SBW in human form, by which using them together allows Francesca to utilize her insane debuffs with good consistency. Though, Francesca alone can work well in shorter contents given some block management, namely Hasla Wars and Ordeal.
289: Ah the sweet chime of powercreep. It's quite obvious that her kit has been designed around the primary difficulties of the current general content, which enables her to completely trivialize the current end game contents (as if these aren't already easy enough).
290: Despite her only being able to buff your leader, his damage buffing capabilities to magic DPSes is completely beyond understanding.
291: Possesses one of the highest hit count numbers in the game. Though, her range is quite an issue in normal PvE settings. A competitive choice for Hasla Wars if you are lacking Lupeows, especially given Kaede is the banner complement.
292: Cloning leader can be very very very useful, and this unique mechanic makes her incredibly flexible and irreplacable at times.
293: A strong and functional DPS in challenge, and does not need a lot of blocks at that. However, her viability is completely crippled if she does not directly kill mobs, and is only functional in challenge due to this. As of right now, her damage isn't quite high enough to warrant consideration.
294: The single most broken buffer for melee physical DPSes. Do note that he does not function too well with most ranged DPSes in challenge due to Pumpking's narrow buffing range, and in stationary situations, only wizards cannot get access to his buffs.
295: A good DPS with some support utility given her ridiculous magical dmg amp. Capable of acting as a primary challenge carry and can phase into speedrun teams given proper supports, but is certainly a bit block hungry.
296: Although his damage numbers isn't quite up to par with Bera, a single 3 chain can provide him with 17 seconds of consistent damage output which renders him one of the least block hungry heroes in game. However, his damage is just not up to par with more recent heroes.
298: Primrose clone, but physical. However, one advantage she has over Primrose is that she does not have any animations while entering stance, which means she gets to use blocks immediately. This makes for a scary burst team in arena when paired with 3 chain chasers.
299: Her damage is among highest in game. Catch is, she has no range and she doesn't move, restricting her challenge capability. On the other hand, she has rather solid mechanics which stands out among the heroes in her damage range, which says something about her future viability.
301:
The basic resource in the game. Can be used to upgrade weapons, feed bread and berries, transfer skills, buy things from popo, inlay or take out sigils, and so on.

Gold may be obtained primarily through friend honor exchanges, quests, fishing, story and challenges stages. It can also be bought in large quantities in the fishing shop, which will always be your main source of gold income. Note that farming gold outside Fishing is not recommended as they are extremely inefficient.

Side note, selling high rarity useless identified sigil in bulk can also be a decent gold income. While there is the option of saving up for a box, what you get is completely RNG, and the box itself already cost a fortune, not to mention the money you lost by not selling those sigil.
302:
Meat should be self explanatory. It is a resource required to play story mode, challenge mode, and raid stages. Meat can be obtained from many sources, including sending honor to friends, quests, colosseum, and may be bought in large quantities from the fishing shop. If you do not have enough meat, the 30-gem meat package from the shop is not a bad deal either.

Although meat seems like an abundant resource at first, when it comes to mid to late game farming, you would begin to realize that meat isn't as plentiful as it seems. You will need meat almost everywhere, and combined with the low drop rate of sigils in challenge and raid, you will certainly need as much of it as you can.
303:
This should also be quite obvious. Keys are used to enter dungeons stages, and sometimes, certain event dungeon stages as well.

Keys can be obtained through daily and weekly quests. They can also be bought from travelling merchant Popo. Popo from episode 6 onwards may sell 10 keys in a single slot.

Hoarding key can be considered in the following situation:
1. You need resu rings => hoard key for fergus ring event
2. You need crystals => hoard key for weekened acceleration dungeon
3. You want to have a high ranking in collection event
305:
Colosseum tickets, as their name suggests, is used to enter colosseum. As colosseum is the only sustainable source of gems in game without paying, this resource can be very valuable when competing for higher percentage brackets.

Apart from the regenerating tickets and from daily quest, where both of which are limited, the only other source of colosseum tickets are from travelling merchant Popo. When you see the phrase "farming Popo", this is often the primary purpose.
307:
Popo is a chance encounter limited time shop which you can find when doing any scenario or challenge stages.

She has a 1/8 chance to appear every time you complete a scenario or challenge stage, but only Popo from Deep Sea and beyond can sell ticket, and Popo from Battlefield and beyond can sell more keys per slot. Later, popo will start selling pages, and challenge popo will sometimes sell you a chest from that challenge mode, at a very reasonable price.

Note that Popo found in Forest and Desert have 4 slots, Popo found in Deep Sea and Volcano have 6 slots, and Popo from Tundra and beyond have 8 slots.

The recommended farming spots for Popo is the highest stage with the lowest meat cost in Tundra (5-8), and Battlefield (6-3). The former is preferred when tickets is prioritized for its lower meat cost, and the latter is preferred when you want more keys.
308:
The semi-premium currency in game. Gems are primarily used to pull for heroes and to expand inventory slots. Do not use gems to reset hero promotions.

Beginners can quickly amass a large amount of it through max levelling heroes they have not maxed before, as well as through various story quests. After the beginner gem pool, the primary source of gem income is colosseum.
309: Honor is used primarily for promoting heroes, and is also a necessary resource for upgrading skills as well. Honor is obtained primarily from the honor dungeon. Excess honor can be be used to buy hero home decorations.
310:
The premium currency in game. Bridget Points can be obtained through daily logins, certain events, and occasionally appears in daily limited time rewards (if you are in global server).

You can use BP to guarantee great success on weapon upgrades and skill transfers, however it is considered a poor usage of the limited currency. It is recommended to save up BPs hero selection tickets. The value of seasonal hero selection ticket is debatable.
312:
Fish Coins can be obtained from fishing (duh), as well as fishing related events and one-time achievements.

You can trade in Fish Coins in for anything in the fishing shop. You should prioritize earning as much as these as you can. It’s a good idea to purchase the 1600 Meat, Gold, and Random Option Ticket. Do save some fish coins to buy gold in case of events such as (sc)hammer time. 

See to your needs for other items.
314:
Arena coins are obtained weekly from arena. The amount you get depends on your ranking. These can also be obtained from winning (20 coins) or losing (10 coins) an arena match, and does not have an acqisition limit.

Due to this nature, one may set up a script to automatically match in arena to exploit this resource but please don't let this be you.

This is a great source of battleloids, pages, fergus point, and many other resources. The 4 star contract it offer has a chance to drop contract only hero, but is not guaranteed.

It is generally best to just use them to buy champion food.
316:
Ordeal coins are obtained after ordeal mode finishes. The amount you get is dependent on your ranking.

These are used to purchase ordeal exclusive emotes, battleloids, pages, fergus points and growth package.

This is a great way to quickly raise your champion level as you can obtain a large number of battleloids through it. The box that cost 100 coins is also a good deal for beginners and end-game players alike.
317:
This is what a champion food looks like. There are 4/5/6 star versions, but they all looks kind of similar. The 3 star version gives 25 points, 4 star - 150 points, 5 star - 250 points, and 6 star - 500 points.

For beginners, like any other hero, you can obtain a gem from max levelling them for the first time.

Combat wise, they are completely useless, so just send them to the champion you want and be done with them.
318:
Iron are primary farmed from world bosses and challenge. Due to the low drop rate of sigils and inheritance items, farming iron in the newest challenge is often considered to be the most effective way to obtain iron.

Iron's only use is to create and forge sould bound weapons, and you will need a great amount when doing so. On top of that, you also need SBW materials.
320:
Randome Weapon Option Tickets are obtained from events, weekly quests, one-time achievements, and can be purchased from fishing shop every week.

They are used to reset the options of SBW, however, due to their random nature, it takes a lot of luck. It is prefered to use these on Collab hero since copies of their SBW cannot be obtained unless you gain a second copy.
322:
Option Ticket are only given out in some events, or can be purchased in the Bridget Shop. It is, however, not a good investment.

Option ticket can be used to change one opton of your SBW to whatever you want. Due to these, they are extremely rare and is prefered to use on SBWs that only need 1 of its option changed.
324:
By Gem Fishing Set, it refers to the Bamboo Rod and Seiren Doll / Rubber Ducky.

It is recommended for a player to first purchase the Seiren Doll from the fishing shop as soon as you can as it is unlocked at Fishing Rank 1. The earlier you buy it and use it, the faster it pays off. The items in the fishing shop are very lucrative. Auto fish overnight for passive fish coin income. It is suggested to use an emulator to avoid destroying your device's battery life.

It should be noted that the fish coin sets aren't completely outclassed when compared to gem set. From the (not very reliable) data gathered from the survey, gem sets are around 20-40% better than fish coin sets. However, it would not be very possible for you to amass 600k fish coins in a short time to immediately make use of the fish coin set, which may severely hinder your progression.

From a long term perspective, the Seiren Doll is definitely a worthy investment. It is up to you, the player, to determine whether you want to save the 99 gems in exchange for a much slower initial progression.

Note that there are zero differences, fish coin income wise, between the Rubber Ducky and Seiren Doll, as the terrain bonuses affects nothing but fish size. For fishing events, the difference is also nonexistent for it takes place in neutral water.
326:
After buying the fishing set, the main use of gems is to purchase contracts from Bridget Shop. This is the primary way for you to obtain new heroes.

The difference between normal contracts and special contracts is that, special contracts have higher rates for the displayed heroes. Always purchase the 10x Consectutive / Special Contracts from the shop for 50 gems as these are not only cheaper than buying 10 individual contracts, but also guarantee a premium 4* hero.

It is suggested to pull a couple of 10x Consectutive / Special Contracts prior to using your Hero Selection Ticket. This may help you to determine your suggested route.

Save your gems for rate ups with heroes you want.
Don't know what you need? Check out the "Picking Heroes" section.
328:
Once you have a stable pool of heroes for PvE and PvC purposes, it is recommended to save your gems for seasonal heroes and potential collabs.

Seasonal limited banners return at approximately the same time every year. There are currently 14 seasonal heroes in total, and they can only be obtained from their respective seasonal limited banners (or with 5000 BP). The list of seasonal heroes and their approximate schedule can be found in the Seasonal Schedule tab.

Although collab dates and contents are impossible to determine ahead of time, going by past patterns, there will usually be 2 or 3 collabs within a given year. Save your gems just in case, as collab teasers will only be shown one week prior.
330: Expand when you believe it is necessary, as it is a permanent upgrade and you will eventually have an use for it. It is generally useful to keep around 10-20 inventory slots, namely hero, weapon, berry, sigil, and book slots, open while farming for resources for convenience sake.
331:
The abovementioned ways are not the only ways you can spend your gems. Rather, they are the only ways that are worth the cost. It is generally advised not to use your gems anywhere else.

Do note that buying the monthly meat pack is not a bad investment. However, the value of which depends on the player's needs, and it is best to rate its worth yourself.
333:
Mana Essences can be obtained from primarily from LoPF, as well as from one-time achievements and through extracting rings.

Their only use is to reroll ring sub slots, however you will need a large amount when doing so.
335:
Flame Essences can sometimes be obtained from LoPF.

These are used to increase the option of rings to its maximum amount.
336:
Manacar Rings are obtained from Manacar World Boss.

The possible subslots for Manacar Rings are:

- Armor Penetration
- Resistance Penetration
- Damage Reduction
- Maximum HP Increase
- Attack Speed
- Accuracy
- Evasion
338:
LoPF rings can be gained in the Legend of Primal Flames. 
The possible subslots for LoPF Rings are:

- (PvE Only) Mercenary EXP (Increases Player Level EXP)
- (PvE Only) Hero EXP (Increases EXP gain for all heroes)
- (PvE Only) Scenario Gold Increase (Increases Gold drops in Stages)
- (PvC Only) Physical Damage Increase
- (PvC Only) Magical Damage Increase
- (PvC Only) Armor Increase
- (PvC Only) Resistance Increase
- (PvC Only) %HP Increase
- (PvC Only) Critical (Chance) Resistance Increase
